note: The owner's profile as data: the questions the harness puts to him (as chat questions), what each answer is stored as, and what the router and the sensitivity guard read from it. A model never writes these questions or their options. A new field is a new row here and a line in profile.py's APPLY table only when the router must read it.

fields.question: What counts as confidential for you? Tasks that touch any of these never leave your own computers. Pick all that apply.

options.label: Personal data about people (names, addresses, ID numbers)

fields.none_label: Nothing in particular: I will say so when something is confidential

fields.question: For a task that touches none of those, what should I assume?

options.label: Ask me each time whether it is public, internal or confidential

fields.question: Cloud models (an API or a subscription) can cost money. What is your stance?

options.label: Only when no local model can do the task

fields.question: When a task fails on a cheaper route, how many times may I move it up to a costlier one without asking you? (0, 1 or 2; steps, not money: no spend limit exists)

Which of your subscriptions may I use automatically? Using one this way runs its command-line tool through your plan without you at the keyboard. The harness does not evaluate the vendor's terms for automated use; reading them is yours. Pick all that apply.
When a local model and a cloud model are equally good, which do you prefer?

options.label: No preference: the best measured one

fields.question: How much detail do you want in what Multi Auto Setup shows you?

options.label: Normal: the facts and what to do next
Detailed: everything, with ids and hashes

fields.question: When local models are otherwise level, whose models should come first in your setup options? The list is the publishers of the models the catalog has verified. This release's default is the owner's own choice.

options.label: General: any task may run there
Private: only local models may run there, never a cloud one
Not for tasks: keep it out of the router

categories_note: A task states which of these it touches (or none, or unsure); the harness derives the level from the profile and asks the owner when it cannot.
